subject: Re: Quantiva Health — model improvement opt-out & subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Benjamin Ross <benjamin.ross@quantiva.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@quantiva.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: Quantiva onboarding — no-train requirement + subprocessor evidence

Hi Sergio / Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week. As Quantiva's security team reviews vendors, two items are blocking our legal review and procurement sign-off: a firm no-training commitment for customer data (including prompts and generated responses) and a current list of all subprocessors with attestations that they will not use Quantiva data to improve models.

Specifically:
- We need language confirming Redwood will not use Quantiva prompts/responses to train, fine-tune, or improve any models (including internal research).
- A CSV or registry extract listing subprocessors (name, role, country) and the latest evidence (SOC2 or equivalent).
- Clarification on caching/logging TTLs and whether any telemetry is sampled for model improvement.

If you already have a standard clause or an addendum for "model improvement opt-out" we can expedite review. Also, please include any evidence you can share under NDA.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our go-live target is end of May.

Best,
Benjamin Ross
Head of Security Programs
Quantiva Health

Attachment: quantiva-security-checklist.pdf (stub)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Benjamin Ross <benjamin.ross@quantiva.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: Quantiva onboarding — no-train requirement + subprocessor evidence

Hi Benjamin — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on the priority items and can provide the artifacts you asked for. Quick summary:

1) No-training option: Redwood offers an explicit "no training / no model improvement" contractual option for customer request streams. That option prevents any prompts, responses, or other customer-provided content from being used to train or tune models. We can provide a DPA addendum with the exact language.

2) Subprocessors: we maintain a live registry and can export a CSV for Quantiva. We'll include role, country, and our latest third-party attestation for each vendor.

3) Telemetry & caching: by default we collect minimal operational telemetry for SLOs (latency, error rates) but do not include customer payloads in model improvement telemetry when the no-training option is active. Caches (prefix/KV) are tenant-scoped and TTLs are configurable — default short-lived (24 hours) for hosted customers, and can be disabled.

I'll loop Monica to share the SOC2 report and the subprocessor export. Karthik is copied to confirm logging/config options for Dedicated/private deployments if you need them.

Next steps I propose:
- Monica uploads the evidence bundle and a DPA addendum draft for your counsel.
- We leave a short window for Quantiva redlines and then sign.
- If helpful, schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk legal/security through the clause.

Options for links and artifacts: https://drive.redwood.internal/quantiva/dpa-draft and https://status.redwood.ai/subprocessors/quantiva-2027

Talk soon,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Accounts — West
Redwood Inference

Benjamin,

Attaching the evidence bundle as discussed and a first-pass DPA addendum that captures the no-training commitment and ownership language. Highlights:
- Clause 4.2 (No-Training): "Redwood shall not use any Customer Data (including prompts and model outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve models under any default or experimental pipeline when the Customer elects the No-Training option."
- Clause 5.1 (Output/IP): "Customer retains all rights to prompts and generated outputs; Redwood disclaims any rights to derive ownership over Customer content."
- Subprocessor appendix: exported CSV is included.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood-subprocessors-2027.csv
- SOC2-report-Type2-2026.pdf
- DPA-quantiva-redlines.pdf (DPA addendum draft)

Notes: SOC2 report is a summary redaction for external sharing; full report can be produced under NDA and via secure portal. If Quantiva needs further attestation about specific subprocessors (e.g., cloud provider encryption boundaries) we can coordinate a short technical Q&A.

If the DPA language looks OK, Sergio can send the DocuSign flow. Otherwise, Sophie can send redlines and we'll respond in the thread.

— Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Benjamin Ross <benjamin.ross@quantiva.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@quantiva.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantiva onboarding — evidence bundle + DPA addendum

Monica, Sergio — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the draft language. A few follow-ups from our counsel:

1) The "No-Training" clause looks good but we want an explicit sentence that mentions "internal research" and "offline experimentation" to prevent ambiguity. Can you add that?
2) We need a statement that confirms logs/sample telemetry will not be exported for model improvement pipelines even in aggregate form without consent.
3) For subprocessors, we asked for a signed attestation for any subprocessor that has access to plaintext customer content — can Redwood provide a short template attestation that subprocessors can sign or a record of attestations you already have?
4) Cross-border: Quantiva is EU-based for the product in scope. Need to confirm that transfers to US subprocessors are done under SCCs (or equivalent) and whether Redwood relies on EU-UK/US frameworks.

Also adding one operational question: what happens to cached KV entries if the customer later requests deletion — do you have purge/erase guarantees and timelines?

If we can get those clarifications and a one–page attestation template by Friday, our procurement team can complete review next week.

Best,
Ben
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Benjamin Ross <benjamin.ross@quantiva.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantiva onboarding — evidence bundle + DPA addendum

Ben — thanks, here are concrete next steps and answers to each of your points: 

1) Wording update: Monica has added a clarifying sentence specifying "internal research and offline experimentation" will be excluded under the No-Training option. See page 2, paragraph 2 of the DPA-quantiva-redlines.pdf.

2) Telemetry assurance: we confirm operational telemetry used for platform health will never be routed into model improvement pipelines for accounts that select No-Training. We'll provide a signed attestation template for telemetry segregation.

3) Subprocessor attestations: attached CSV includes current subprocessors. For any subprocessor with potential content access, we will provide a short signed attestation (vendor name, scope, date, signer). We'll drop a template into the shared Drive today.

4) Cross-border transfers: Redwood relies on standard SCCs for EU->US transfers for our hosted service and supports customer-managed keys for additional controls. Monica can add the exact SCC references in the DPA if required.

5) Cache/delete: tenant-scoped KV/prefix caches are purgeable on request — standard deletion timeline is 72 hours after verified request; we can tighten that for Enterprise contracts. We'll include the purge SLA in the addendum.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: we upload the attestation template and final DPA draft to the Drive link.
- By Thu (5/12): Quantiva counsel returns redlines.
- By Fri (5/19): execute DPA via DocuSign and confirm deployment schedule.

If you'd like, let's set a 30-minute call Wed 5/11 10:00 PT to walk the legal/security team through the attestation language. I'll send a calendar invite pending your confirmation.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you over the finish line.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Accounts — West
Redwood Inference
